skills.title: The Buffett Owner's Lens
skills.tagline: Turn a business or capital decision into owner economics, opportunity cost, downside protection, and a clear action.
skills.whenToUse: Use when a consequential business, investment, acquisition, hiring, or resource-allocation decision needs a patient owner-oriented analysis.
skills.source: Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letters, 1977-2024, by Warren E. Buffett
skills.problemHint: Describe the decision, the underlying economics, the available alternatives, the people involved, and what could cause permanent loss.
skills.corePrinciple: Act as a long-term owner. Understand the economic engine, compare it with the best alternative, protect the ability to continue, and act only when the case is both intelligible and favorable.

framework.title: Bound the circle
framework.body: State what is understood, what is assumed, and what is outside the circle of competence. Do not hide uncertainty inside a forecast.

framework.title: Translate to owner economics
framework.body: Identify sustainable cash generation, required reinvestment, pricing power, capital intensity, and the factors that determine long-term value.

framework.title: Audit moat and people
framework.body: Test the durability of the competitive advantage and the integrity, ability, incentives, and owner orientation of the people in charge.

framework.title: Compare opportunity costs
framework.body: Name the single best alternative, including inaction and liquidity. Evaluate the choice against that alternative, not against an empty baseline.

framework.title: Protect the downside
framework.body: Stress financing, counterparties, reputation, and assumptions. Reject any avoidable path that can force action or create permanent loss.

framework.title: Decide and monitor
framework.body: Give a clear act, wait, pass, or investigate judgment. Name the evidence that would change it and correct mistakes promptly.

antiPatterns: Treating a market price, forecast, or peer action as a substitute for independent value judgment.
Using leverage or fragile obligations to make an otherwise ordinary return look attractive.
Recommending a named security, price target, market timing call, or personalized asset allocation.
Producing false precision where the economics are not understood.
skills.outputShape: Return: Decision in one sentence; Circle of competence; Owner economics; Moat and management; Best alternative; Downside and liquidity; Recommendation; Evidence that would change the decision.
skills.closingQuote: A small chance of distress or disgrace cannot, in our view, be offset by a large chance of extra returns.

skills.title: Owner Earnings
skills.tagline: Convert reported accounting results into the cash an owner can take out without weakening the business.
skills.whenToUse: Use when evaluating a business model, budget, acquisition, project, or financial statement whose reported profit may differ from economic cash generation.
skills.source: Berkshire Hathaway 1986 shareholder letter by Warren E. Buffett
skills.sourceAnchor: 1986 letter, purchase-price accounting and owner earnings discussion
skills.problemHint: Provide reported earnings, non-cash charges, working-capital needs, maintenance spending, and any growth spending you can separate.
skills.corePrinciple: Owner earnings approximate reported earnings plus non-cash charges, less the average capital spending and working capital required to maintain unit volume and competitive position.

framework.title: Start with reported earnings
framework.body: Use the most representative after-tax operating result available and flag one-time or non-operating items.

framework.title: Add back real non-cash charges
framework.body: Add depreciation, amortization, and similar charges only when they did not consume current cash and are not disguising a recurring economic cost.

framework.title: Estimate maintenance needs
framework.body: Subtract the normal capital expenditure and working capital needed to preserve current volume, service, and competitive strength.

framework.title: Separate growth
framework.body: Show discretionary expansion investment separately so the user can judge its likely incremental return.

framework.title: Use a range
framework.body: Present conservative, base, and optimistic estimates when maintenance needs are uncertain. Explain the variable that drives the range.

antiPatterns: Treating every non-cash charge as economically irrelevant.
Calling all capital expenditure growth investment.
Using EBITDA as cash available to owners without testing reinvestment needs.
Hiding estimation uncertainty behind a single precise number.
skills.outputShape: Return a compact bridge from reported earnings to estimated owner earnings, followed by maintenance assumptions, growth investment, sensitivity range, and the key unresolved question.

skills.title: Circle of Competence
skills.tagline: Draw the boundary between what can be evaluated, what must be learned, and what should simply be passed.
skills.whenToUse: Use when a decision feels exciting but depends on unfamiliar technology, economics, regulation, behavior, or forecasting.
skills.source: Berkshire Hathaway 1996 shareholder letter by Warren E. Buffett
skills.problemHint: Describe the opportunity, your direct experience, the variables you can estimate, and the assumptions supplied by other people.
skills.corePrinciple: The size of the circle matters less than knowing its boundary. A clean pass is a successful decision when the important economics cannot be evaluated reliably.

framework.title: Name the engine
framework.body: Explain in plain language how value is created, captured, and converted into cash.

framework.title: List decisive variables
framework.body: Identify the few factors that determine the result and mark which ones can be estimated from evidence.

framework.title: Separate knowledge from borrowed confidence
framework.body: Label direct knowledge, verified facts, assumptions, and claims that depend on an expert or promoter.

framework.title: Test predictability
framework.body: Ask whether the relevant economics can be estimated across a useful time horizon without heroic assumptions.

framework.title: Choose learn, partner, or pass
framework.body: Define the cheapest evidence that could expand the circle, the trustworthy expert needed, or the reason to decline.

antiPatterns: Mistaking familiarity with a product for understanding its economics.
Expanding the circle because others appear confident or prices are moving.
Treating uncertainty as a weakness that must be concealed.
Giving personalized investment instructions when the proper result is an evidence plan or pass.
skills.outputShape: Return: Inside the circle; Outside the circle; Decisive unknowns; Cheapest learning tests; Learn, partner, or pass; Revisit condition.
skills.closingQuote: The size of that circle is not very important; knowing its boundaries, however, is vital.

skills.title: The Retained Earnings Test
skills.tagline: Make every retained dollar compete against distribution and the best alternative use of capital.
skills.whenToUse: Use when deciding whether to reinvest profits, fund a new initiative, acquire a company, repay debt, hold cash, or return capital.
skills.source: Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letters by Warren E. Buffett
skills.sourceAnchor: 1980, 1982, and 1984 letters, retained earnings and capital allocation
skills.problemHint: Provide the amount available, each candidate use, expected incremental economics, time horizon, downside, and evidence from prior allocations.
skills.corePrinciple: Management should retain a dollar only when it has a reasonable prospect of creating more than a dollar of long-term value after risk and opportunity cost.

framework.title: Inventory every use
framework.body: Include maintenance, organic growth, acquisitions, debt reduction, liquidity, and distribution. Do not let a preferred project become the default.

framework.title: Separate maintenance from growth
framework.body: Fund what preserves the current franchise before claiming that the remaining spend creates new value.

framework.title: Estimate incremental returns
framework.body: Judge the next dollar, not the historical average. Include execution risk, time to payoff, and future capital needs.

framework.title: Compare with the hurdle
framework.body: Use the best available alternative and a margin of safety, not an arbitrary internal target.

framework.title: Audit the record
framework.body: Compare prior promises with actual incremental earnings, cash generation, and value creation.

framework.title: Allocate and review
framework.body: Rank uses, set a review date, and specify the evidence that stops further funding.

antiPatterns: Retaining cash merely because management controls it.
Using average company returns to justify a weak incremental project.
Ignoring dilution, integration costs, or follow-on capital.
Rewarding project size instead of value created per dollar.
skills.outputShape: Return a ranked capital-allocation table with amount, incremental return logic, time horizon, downside, confidence, and stop condition, followed by the recommended allocation.

skills.title: Build a Financial Fortress
skills.tagline: Stress obligations, counterparties, and liquidity so no ordinary shock can force a permanent loss.
skills.whenToUse: Use before taking debt, signing guarantees or long-duration contracts, setting cash reserves, or evaluating whether a plan can survive a severe interruption.
skills.source: Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letters by Warren E. Buffett
skills.problemHint: List cash, recurring inflows, fixed obligations, maturities, covenants, collateral, counterparties, and the worst plausible interruption.
skills.corePrinciple: Liquidity and reputation are survival assets. Never accept a small chance of forced failure in exchange for an unnecessary increase in expected return.

framework.title: Map all cash calls
framework.body: List operating needs, debt service, collateral, guarantees, commitments, and obligations hidden in contracts or subsidiaries.

framework.title: Stress timing
framework.body: Assume revenue falls, refinancing closes, asset prices drop, and several counterparties weaken at the same time.

framework.title: Trace the chain
framework.body: Follow exposures through counterparties and affiliates. A promise is only as strong as the party that must perform under stress.

framework.title: Protect essential liquidity
framework.body: Reserve enough cash and near-cash resources to meet obligations without relying on asset sales, new credit, or favorable markets.

framework.title: Remove asymmetric ruin
framework.body: Restructure, cap, collateralize, shorten, insure, or reject obligations whose downside can end the game.

framework.title: Define triggers
framework.body: Set early warning indicators and actions that preserve optionality before a covenant or cash deadline removes it.

antiPatterns: Assuming several correlated risks cannot arrive together.
Treating access to refinancing as permanent liquidity.
Optimizing idle cash while ignoring survival value.
Accepting unlimited downside for a modest recurring benefit.
skills.outputShape: Return: Obligations map; Stress scenario; Counterparty chain; Minimum liquidity; Ruin paths to remove; Early triggers; Fortress verdict.
skills.closingQuote: A small chance of distress or disgrace cannot, in our view, be offset by a large chance of extra returns.

skills.title: The Berkshire Acquisition Filter
skills.tagline: Screen an acquisition for understandable economics, durable advantage, trustworthy management, price, financing, and fit before deal momentum takes over.
skills.whenToUse: Use when evaluating a company acquisition, strategic partnership, major vendor commitment, or other transaction that can become emotionally difficult to stop.
skills.source: Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letters by Warren E. Buffett
skills.problemHint: Provide the target's economics, management, moat, price, financing, integration assumptions, alternatives, and the incentives of everyone advocating the deal.
skills.corePrinciple: A transaction should work because the target is understandable, durable, well managed, and sensibly priced, not because leverage, synergy language, or deal momentum makes it appear so.

framework.title: Write the owner case
framework.body: Explain how the target earns cash, why customers stay, what capital it needs, and why its economics should endure.

framework.title: Assess management and autonomy
framework.body: Determine whether the current managers are able, trustworthy, motivated to remain, and compatible with the intended level of control.

framework.title: Value without synergies
framework.body: Estimate conservative stand-alone owner earnings and value before adding integration or cross-selling claims.

framework.title: Audit transaction incentives
framework.body: List how executives, bankers, consultants, and sellers benefit if the transaction closes and who is paid if it fails.

framework.title: Test financing and opportunity cost
framework.body: Compare cash, debt, and equity consideration, including dilution, fragility, and the best alternative use of each resource.

framework.title: Set the walk-away line
framework.body: Define maximum price, unacceptable terms, diligence failures, and the person empowered to stop the process.

antiPatterns: Starting with the desired closing date and back-solving the economics.
Paying for synergies before they are achieved.
Using cheap debt or inflated equity to excuse a weak business.
Letting advisors whose fee depends on closing frame the final decision.
skills.outputShape: Return a pass or proceed scorecard covering business, moat, management, stand-alone value, incentives, financing, opportunity cost, walk-away conditions, and final verdict.
